### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/profiles.mdx`  _(via PermissionSetSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via PermissionSetSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via PermissionSetSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via PermissionSetSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dd9a08d9d1bf4a5aa5f37078d39a0f45e84d805b` — the merge of head `aeb3c973e6549ffa66d66b05601f30b3af3d8cd2` into base `df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dd9a08d9d1bf4a5aa5f37078d39a0f45e84d805b && git checkout dd9a08d9d1bf4a5aa5f37078d39a0f45e84d805b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1 aeb3c973e6549ffa66d66b05601f30b3af3d8cd2 && git checkout -B drift-repro df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1 && git merge --no-ff aeb3c973e6549ffa66d66b05601f30b3af3d8cd2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `854b36e4fc013ffc31164226c32f2d3c29c7b67d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts + none

No file in this diff implements or enforces the describe: the code it describes (`permissionSetHoldersMeet` in `packages/core/src/permission-set-holders.ts`, the registry's `securityCatalogHoldersOtherThan`, the save door's `permissionSetNameCollisionRefusal` and `refusePackagedBaseOverride`) is outside the diff and was read on `main`, not reviewed. `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx` was read sentence by sentence against the same code because the card rides it on this PR; the generated row, the changeset and that page are otherwise the lane seat's ACCEPT.

Inputs read: card #32758 body and its five comments (6837778026, 6847899833, claim 6881630925, report 6882046858, seat answers 6882071328), PR #33384 body, file list (4 files, +26 / -6) and net diff against `main`, PR #32742 as context, the check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged, right.** `name` stays `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema`; only the `.describe()` string, the JSDoc line and a `//` comment move. No value parses differently.
- **Public surface: one published string changes, right.** The describe ships in `@objectstack/spec` `dist` and projects to `content/docs/references/security/permission.mdx`. The generated `name` row on this head is character for character the describe string (compared on the head's two blobs). No other tracked projection carries the old string.
- **No rule, schema, gate or runtime file in the diff.** `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no door answers differently.
- **Docs page:** one bullet of `permission-sets.mdx` reworded; no anchor, route or example changes.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/32758-permission-set-name-describe.md` is `@objectstack/spec: patch` and carries both declaration lines (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`), matching the PR body. Patch is the right level: a description string in the published package changes and nothing an author can write or a consumer can read by shape moves. `skip-changeset` would have been wrong (the string is in `dist`). `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.

Clause-②: no — agreed. Neither a widening nor a narrowing: the text now states what #32742 (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`) already shipped.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Report `open_questions` Q1** (migration entry 18 `reason`) and **Q2** (`customization-package.ts:251-252` gloss): answered B by the seat (6882071328), follow-up card #33388, open. Not in this PR. Answered.
- **Out-of-scope class-b finding** (objectql `registry.ts` refusal sentences): card #33389, open. Answered.
- **Carrier-none notes** (`security-service.ts:419` stays true for a platform-namespace set; ADR and dogfood comments): accepted as noted by the seat. I read `:419`'s premise against the predicate: a holder in `base`, `system` or `sys` meets every holder, so "unique in the security catalog" holds for it.
- **Deviation: the `//` comment line** added above the field. Inside the claimed file surface ("the `name` JSDoc and describe only" read with the field's own comment block); comment-only. Accepted.
- **Deviation: PR opened with no labels.** The head now carries `documentation`, `size/s`, `tooling` from Auto Label. Nothing to rule.
- **Gates.** The dev's local loop left `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED and re-ran `check:generated` alone. On this head, at the last read for this record, 27 check-runs concluded success (among them Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Build Core, Build Docs, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint & Repo Gates and every `Lint ·` job, Check Documentation Links, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards), 10 were skipped, **none failed**, and 28 had **not concluded**: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16. This record therefore does not carry a verdict for those families; the landing seat reads their conclusions before it lands. A text-only diff gives no reason to expect a failure there, but that is an expectation, not a measurement.
- **Docs drift advisory** (PR comment 6882057435) lists `content/docs/permissions/profiles.mdx` through the `PermissionSetSchema` symbol. Read on this head: it carries no sentence about a set name's uniqueness. Nothing owed.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`** — judged against the ruling it implements (card #32758's TO, ADR-0150 D2/D9 as #32742 shipped them) and its first consumer, the predicate on `main`.

Sentence by sentence against `permissionSetHoldersMeet(incomingNamespace, holderNamespace, name)`:

| The describe says | The code on `main` | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "a name has one holder per namespace, so packages of two namespaces may each hold a set of one name" | returns false only when both namespaces are declared, neither is shareable, they differ, and the name is not platform-requested | yes, as the name rule (see N1) |
| "two packages of one namespace … share one set" | last line: `incomingNamespace === holderNamespace` | yes |
| "a package with no namespace" | `!incomingNamespace or !holderNamespace` returns true | yes, on either side |
| "a platform package (base, system, sys)" | `PERMISSION_SET_SHARED_NAMESPACES` = base, system, sys, on either side | yes (see N2) |
| "the environment" | not the predicate's: the registry adds the environment holder without asking it (`opts.environment`), and the save door's `meets` answers true for `holder === null` or `written === null` | yes |
| "the platform-requested guest_portal" | `isPlatformRequestedBareName('permission', name)`; the list on `main` is `['guest_portal']` alone | yes |

Attempts to break it:

- **Co-owners of one namespace**: meet, second refused. Agrees.
- **No namespace beside a namespaced holder, and two with none**: meet. Agrees.
- **`sys` + `crm`, either order**: meet. Agrees. ADR-0150 D2 lets two packages of a shareable namespace hold one behavioural name under the sibling predicate; the describe correctly follows the stricter permission-set predicate, not D2's general wording.
- **`guest_portal` from `crm` and `hr`**: meets whatever the namespaces. Agrees.
- **A built-in permission-set name**: #32742 lists it among the one-holder cases, the describe does not. `BUILT_IN_SECURITY_CATALOG_NAMES.permission` is the empty set on `main`, so there is no such name to list. The omission is right.
- **Positions and capabilities** (the `//` comment's last clause): the registry narrows only where `type === 'permission'`; `position.zod.ts:84` keeps "unique within the security catalog the environment serves", still true. Agrees.

Findings:

- **N1 — nit.** "packages of two namespaces may each hold a set of one name" is true of the name rule and of two packages that ship their sets (install gate and item seam), and it is not the whole answer at the metadata save door. There, (a) a set another package STORES holds its name whatever the namespaces (`meets` includes `storedPackages.has(holder)`; 422 `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`), the clause the save door's own sentence ends on ("and a set another package stores holds its name") and the describe drops; and (b) a shipped set that registered its item seals the bare name against any undeclared save (`isSealedManagedItem(type, name)` takes no package; 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`), which is what the dev's own probe measured for the pair. The PR body's "the holder list is the one #32742's save-door sentence states" is therefore one clause short. Graded nit, not should-fix: the sentence says "may", it states the rule the predicate implements, the schema's readers are package authors whose sets ship, the guide's wording on the same point is "ship" and is exact, and the stored limit is a declared temporary one with its own card (#32780, open). Accepted deviation; if the describe is touched again, "may each ship" closes it.
- **N2 — nit.** "a platform package (base, system, sys)" lists namespaces as though they were packages; the predicate judges the holder's namespace. It is the save door's own shipped wording, so the two texts agree with each other. Accepted deviation.
- **N3 — nit.** The `//` block still opens "so a name is one item in the security catalog the environment serves" (ADR-0131 D3) and is corrected only by the sentence the PR appends. Reads as a history followed by its amendment; a source comment, not published. Accepted deviation.

**`content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`** (read, the card's second target):

- "a permission set takes no override (ADR-0146 D6)": `permission` is classified `excluded`, basis `adr_0146_d6_security_catalog`, cited as "ADR-0146 D6" by `judgeOverrideWrite`. Holds.
- "a set of the shipped set's name saved into the pair is refused like an edit of the set itself (`403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`)": an undeclared save reaches `refusePackagedBaseOverride`, which throws `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / 403 for a sealed name when the named package is writable (the pair is); a declared one is refused by `judgeOverrideWrite` and thrown with the same code and status. The page's own preceding sentence gives the same code for an edit through the metadata API. Holds, and it is the reason that survives #32742: the pair's namespace differs from its base's, so the name rule alone would no longer refuse it.
- "identified by its package and name (ADR-0150 D2)": D2's identity is `(package id, type, name)`. Holds; the page's `:268` cites D4 (the runtime keys) for the same statement, and both citations are right.
- "packages of two namespaces may each ship a set of one name, each granted by its own package and name": the grant's `permission_set_package` column, described at `:268-275` of the same page. Holds.
- "Positions and capabilities keep one name per deployment": holds (above).
- **N4 — nit.** The page's one-holder list leaves out the environment, which the describe names and which meets every holder at both doors. The sentence is about packages, so it is not false, but the two texts of this PR differ by that one member. Prose face: fixable here without a delta review, or left.
- **N5 — nit.** Eleven lines above the new text, outside the diff, the page still says "a grant names its set by name (`sys_user_permission_set.permission_set`)". True of that column and incomplete beside "granted by its own package and name". Prose face, follow-up or left.

No must-fix, no should-fix. The describe, its generated row and the guide state what the predicate and the two refusals on `main` do in every case the card names.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-yngygz`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5mswnWm181XgYcCUag`

**VERDICT: PASS**
